title: autotune: default batching/caching + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ethan Chen
description: Introduces autotune defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, a set of curated quantization profiles per model family, and a first-pass unit-economics CLI/console export. Motivation: reduce per-token cost for common workloads with safe defaults while exposing measurable econ impact to customers and SRE. This PR bundles three tightly-related deliverables: 1) runtime: default batching/caching heuristics and an opt-out flag, safe for low-latency paths; 2) model-profiles: curated quantization presets (8-bit, 4-bit where validated) with compatibility metadata and fallback rules; 3) tooling: unit-econ exporter and small console payload to show estimated cost savings by model/profile. Includes perf benchmarks, rollout plan, and upgrade notes. Checklist: ensure backward compatibility with pinned model versions, include canary rollout config, add unit and integration tests, update docs and release notes. Related Linear: ENG-4291 ENG-4310.

review_comments: Maya: Can we guarantee no regression on 99th p latency for small payloads? please add canary config.
Ethan: Added a canary target and added a safety check that disables batching below 32 tokens to protect p99.
Lina: Quant profiles look good but add a clear fallback path for models without validated 4-bit kernels.
Ethan: Added fallback rules in profiles and a runtime compatibility check that logs and falls back to 8-bit when needed.
release_notes: Default autotune: batching and KV-prefix caching enabled by default for standard workloads; curated quantization profiles available; unit-econ export adds visibility into estimated per-token savings. Can be disabled by request-level flags.
performance_summary: Canary benchmarks on standard chat workload showed median cost reduction of 22% and p90 token cost reduction of 18% with negligible latency impact (p50 +1.2ms, p90 +3.5ms) for CPU fallback paths; GPU paths saw up to 30% unit cost drop when 4-bit profiles validated. Rollout plan includes 2% canary -> 20% -> 100% with automated rollback on error rate or p99 degradation >5%.
